limitations: Results apply to the recorded source and artifact identities; they do not change qualification of published v0.7.0 installers.
Local plugin catalogs and unchanged-code manifest updates do not qualify public plugin distribution, a published upgrade or API 2/3 migration.
Fresh shared EDA cluster-app installation, NSP Kafka OAuth, other vendor versions/policies and OS process sandbox enforcement were not qualified.

Native installer recovery uses published 0.6.0 as baseline and unreleased 0.0.0-dev as candidate. Candidate mode starts with the pre-restart baseline backup and does not claim baseline restart passed.
Linux installer recovery uses the extracted AppImage payload; FUSE and desktop launcher integration were not qualified.
Same-account backup restoration does not establish cross-account credential transfer, lost credential-store recovery, downgrade or plugin rollback.

applicationSourceEquivalence.scope: Application src, all plugin source and root npm manifests/lockfile have identical Git objects across the passing native/plugin runs and integrated merged main. Test and documentation trees differ; this does not retroactively qualify different published releases.
